original_question: For the standard cladogram drawing of DTCS(n), study the drawn width profile process W(h), h >= 0, where W(h) counts the number of vertical line segments that cross the strip (h, h+1), equivalently the number of clades with drawing height at most h that arise from splits of clades with drawing height at least h+1.
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the drawn-cladogram width-profile question in §9.4 of the current arXiv version of the paper, which in v2 appeared verbatim as Open Problem 12 in §7.1: study the width profile process of the standard cladogram drawing of DTCS(n). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2303.02529))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right object almost exactly: it is about DTCS(n), the standard cladogram drawing, the width-profile process W(h), and the paper's two equivalent descriptions of W(h) as either the number of vertical lines crossing (h,h+1) or the number of relevant clades determined by draw-height thresholds. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
missing_details: DTCS(n) should be defined explicitly: starting from the root clade [n], each clade of size m >= 2 is split into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i) = m / (2 h_{m-1} i (m-i)) for 1 <= i <= m-1, where h_{m-1} = sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/j. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The 'standard cladogram drawing' should be made explicit: all leaves are placed at level 0, and draw-height is defined recursively by dh(leaf)=0 and, for a split gamma -> (gamma_1, gamma_2), dh(gamma)=1+max(dh(gamma_1), dh(gamma_2)). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

It should be stated that draw-height depends on the shape of the subtree, not only on its size; this is part of the paper's intended scope for the problem. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the process should really be indexed by n, i.e. W_n(h), since the random cladogram comes from DTCS(n). The paper writes W(h) because n is fixed in context. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The counted objects should be identified as vertical line segments in the cladogram representation, or equivalently child clades gamma' with dh(gamma') <= h that are created by splitting a parent clade gamma with dh(gamma) >= h+1. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

Your draft does not say that this is posed by the paper as an open-ended characterization problem; the paper does not prescribe a specific asymptotic, limit theorem, or normalization here, so the refined question should stay at that narrow level. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
refined_question: In the discrete-time critical splitting tree DTCS(n), defined by recursively splitting each m-leaf clade into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/(2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)) for 1 <= i <= m-1, draw the tree as a standard cladogram with all leaves at level 0 and draw-height defined recursively by dh(leaf)=0 and dh(gamma)=1+max{dh(gamma_1),dh(gamma_2)} for each split gamma -> (gamma_1,gamma_2). For this drawn cladogram, characterize the width-profile process W_n(h), h >= 0, where W_n(h) is the number of vertical line segments crossing the interval (h,h+1). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each h >= 0, characterize W_n(h) as the number of clades gamma' with draw-height dh(gamma') <= h that arise as children in a split of a parent clade gamma with dh(gamma) >= h+1. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
justification: The nearest official target is not one of the foundational results but the paper's later drawn-cladogram question: the authors first define DTCS(n), then explain the cladogram convention and recursive draw-height, and finally ask exactly about the associated width profile process. In the current arXiv version this appears in §9.4 as an unnumbered question; in v2 it is Open Problem 12 in §7.1, with wording that matches your draft very closely. Hence the faithful rewrite is to keep the question narrowly on the width profile of the standard cladogram representation, without broadening it to total drawn length or to generic tree-profile questions. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
